enonce_markdown: In a directed writing task, what does **slanting** mean?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

In directed writing you do not report everything. You choose the relevant points and shape them for the purpose, the reader and the form asked for in the task.

### Solution

Slanting is the skill of choosing and presenting the points so that they serve the aim of the task (to persuade, to warn, to report...) and fit the reader. The answer is **a)**.

- b) Copying every point earns no credit: irrelevant points must be left out.
- c) and d) have nothing to do with the meaning of the word in this exam.

choix.texte: selecting and presenting the points so that they serve the purpose of the task and suit the reader
copying every point of the passage in the order given
writing the answer in a sloping handwriting
correcting all the spelling mistakes of the passage

enonce_markdown: A directed writing task says: *"Write in ONE paragraph of not more than 100 words."* Which answer obeys this instruction?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Check three things in the instruction: the number of paragraphs, the word limit, and the form (continuous writing, not notes).

### Solution

The task asks for one paragraph, at most 100 words, in continuous writing. Only **c) one paragraph of 95 words** respects all three conditions.

- a) has two paragraphs.
- b) exceeds the limit by 20 words.
- d) is a list, not a paragraph.

choix.texte: A list of bullet points of 90 words

enonce_markdown: You are the head prefect. You must write a talk persuading pupils to keep the school compound clean. Which of the following points from your notes is the **least relevant** and should be left out?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For each point, ask: does it give a reason, a bad effect or a way to help the pupils keep the compound clean? If not, leave it out.

### Solution

A talk to persuade pupils needs reasons and encouragement. The date and the founders of the school (**b**) do not help to persuade anyone to keep the compound clean.

- a) and c) give harmful effects of dirt.
- d) gives a reward that encourages the pupils.

choix.texte: The school was built by a mission in 1975.
Plastic bags thrown from windows block the drains.
The cleanest class will receive a prize each month.

enonce_markdown: You are writing a talk to persuade villagers to send girls to school. One point in your notes says: *"Some families say school fees are too high for girls."* Which sentence is the **best slanted** use of this point?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Slanting means turning every point towards the purpose of the task. For a persuasive talk, an objection is mentioned only to answer it.

### Solution

The talk must persuade villagers to send girls to school. Sentence **c)** accepts the objection but turns it into an argument for education.

- a) argues against the purpose of the talk.
- b) and d) only repeat the problem and give no persuasion.

choix.texte: Many families think girls cost too much, so they should stay at home.
Fees are high in many schools.
Although the fees seem high, an educated girl will later earn money and support her family, so schooling is a good investment.

enonce_markdown:
You are the president of the Health Club of your school. Using ONLY the relevant points from the following notes, write ONE paragraph of not more than 60 words to persuade your schoolmates to wash their hands regularly.

- Dirty hands carry germs that cause diarrhoea and cholera.
- The school canteen sells groundnuts and doughnuts.
- Washing with soap for twenty seconds removes most germs.
- Two buckets with taps stand beside the toilets.
- The club was founded in 2015.
- Sick pupils miss lessons and fall behind.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Select the points that serve the purpose (to persuade), rewrite them in your own words, address the readers directly, and respect the paragraph and word limits.

### Solution

**Model answer (54 words)**

Dear schoolmates, dirty hands carry germs that cause diarrhoea and cholera, and sick pupils miss lessons and fall behind. Yet washing with soap for twenty seconds removes most of these germs. Two buckets with taps stand beside the toilets, so nobody has an excuse. Wash your hands before eating and after using the toilet.

**Why this works.** The paragraph keeps the points that give a reason (germs cause diarrhoea and cholera; sick pupils miss lessons), the method (soap for twenty seconds) and the facility (buckets with taps). It leaves out the items sold at the canteen and the year the club was founded, because they do not persuade anyone to wash their hands. It speaks directly to the schoolmates, ends with a call to action and stays under 60 words.

**Marking guide.** Content: 3 to 5 relevant points; Slanting: persuasive tone and direct address; Expression: own words, one paragraph, no copying of whole bullets.

enonce_markdown:
You are the secretary of the Bokwai Farmers' Cooperative. Read what was said at today's meeting. Write ONE paragraph of not more than 70 words reporting ONLY the decisions taken about the new storage shed. Use reported style (no direct speech and no names of speakers except Mr Tabi).

- Chairman: Welcome, everybody. Mr Ekema is absent with apologies.
- Mbi: I propose that each member pays 5,000 FCFA for the shed.
- Atem: My cousin sells cement cheaply, but I think his sand is poor.
- Members: Agreed on 5,000 FCFA, to be paid before 30 November.
- Chairman: Mr Tabi, who is a mason, will supervise the building.
- Fon: The rain last week spoilt my maize.
- Members: Agreed that Mr Tabi supervises.
- Chairman: The shed will be built beside the cooperative office, and work begins in December.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Minutes record decisions, not conversation. Keep only what was decided, turn it into reported style (passive and future forms) and leave out greetings, absentees and private remarks.

### Solution

**Model answer (44 words)**

It was resolved that each member pay 5,000 FCFA towards the new storage shed before 30 November. Members also agreed that Mr Tabi, a mason, should supervise the construction. The shed will be built beside the cooperative office, and work will begin in December.

**Why this works.** Three decisions are recorded: the contribution of 5,000 FCFA with its deadline, the supervision by Mr Tabi, and the site and starting date of the work. The welcome, the absence of Mr Ekema, Atem's remark about his cousin (a comment, not a decision) and Fon's complaint about the rain are left out. The verbs ("was resolved", "agreed", "will be built") are those of minutes, and no speaker is quoted.

**Common mistakes.** Copying the dialogue; keeping the speakers' names and direct speech; including the absentee or the maize; going over 70 words.
